criteria.text: Given the Command Center, when it is opened, then every tab is reachable and every card drills down one level.
Given sample mode, when any tab is shown, then the sample data is visibly labelled as sample.

Given the Command Center, when any tab renders, then .colaberry/plan.json and .colaberry/progress.json are both committed in this repo and every tab reads its content from them at runtime rather than from hard-coded values.
Given the Command Center, when any tab is shown, then .colaberry/manifest.json is committed in this repo and every tab shows how old that data is and warns when the age exceeds a week.
Trust — no tab shows a number, a connection or a result the project has not actually produced.
Given a customer, when they access the field availability page, then they see a list of available fields.
Given a field is booked, when a customer views availability, then the field is not shown.
Trust: All field availability views are logged with timestamps.

stories.notes: In-memory field data only (no DB yet, per this story's scope). All 3 criteria verified via automated tests (backend unit/route/logging tests, frontend component tests) and a live browser check via headless Chrome against both dev servers.

criteria.text: Given a customer selects a field and time, when they confirm booking, then the booking is recorded.
Given a field is already booked, when a customer tries to book it, then they receive a conflict message.
Trust: All bookings are logged with customer details and timestamps.

stories.notes: In-memory booking store (no DB yet, per this story's scope). Idempotent create: an identical repeat request from the same customer returns the existing booking instead of erroring or duplicating; a genuine conflict (different customer or non-matching overlapping time) returns 409. All 3 criteria verified via automated tests (backend unit/route tests, frontend interaction tests using userEvent) plus manual curl checks and a live browser check against real dev servers. 2026-09-22 (session CC-20260922-r5kn, via /close-out-story): re-ran verification on booking-form error-path test coverage (200/400/500 response handling) that had been logged in PROGRESS.md by session CC-20260910-n8wc on 2026-09-10 but never committed. All 3 criteria still hold: frontend 6/6 BookingForm tests passing, backend 32/32 bookings tests passing, both typechecks clean. Committed now to close the gap between the log and git history.

criteria.text: Given a customer asks a question, when the AI assistant processes it, then the customer receives a relevant answer.
Given a customer asks a question outside the AI's knowledge, when the AI assistant processes it, then the customer is informed that the question cannot be answered.
Trust: Given a customer interaction, when the AI assistant responds, then the interaction is logged in the audit trail.

stories.notes: Built as a deterministic, rules-based Q&A engine (same honest-substitution reasoning as STORY-006, and directly parallel to the Command Center's own kbChat.js from earlier in this build) - no LLM/AI API credentials exist in this environment, and adding an external AI dependency is a decision reserved for the user. REQ-004 explicitly scopes this to 'pricing and availability', so anything outside that is honestly declined via the same keyword-matching engine - that decline IS acceptance criterion 2, not a shortcoming. Every answer is grounded in real fieldsService data, never fabricated. Widened auditTrailService's entityType/action unions a third time ('ai_interaction'/'answered') - same general-purpose extension pattern as STORY-012. Caught and fixed a real precision bug during manual testing, before formalizing tests: 'book' in the availability keyword pattern caused pricing-only questions containing the word 'book' (e.g. 'how much to book a field?') to get an unnecessarily combined pricing+availability answer; removed it since there's already a dedicated booking flow elsewhere in the app and 'book' is too generic a signal for availability intent specifically. All 3 criteria and all 3 named failure paths verified via automated tests, manual curl (which is what surfaced the keyword bug), and a live DOM check confirming all four nav tabs render together.

criteria.text: Given a refund request, when it is flagged as important, then it is sent to a human for approval.
Given a complaint is received, when it is flagged as important, then it is sent to a human for approval.
Trust: All escalations to humans are logged with timestamps and decision outcomes.

stories.notes: Every valid refund/complaint request is escalated to a human (REQ-008 treats refunds/complaints themselves as the important decisions, no separate triage story exists yet to do finer filtering). In-memory store, no DB yet, same deliberate scope choice as STORY-001/002. Both creation and decision are idempotent: an identical repeat request or an identical repeat decision does not double-create or double-process (double-processing an approval is a real double-refund risk, not just a nicety here). A conflicting second decision (different outcome or decider) on an already-decided escalation is rejected (409), not silently overwritten. All 3 criteria verified via automated tests plus manual curl checks and a live check against real dev servers.

criteria.text: Given a new booking overlaps an existing one, when the system checks, then it identifies a conflict.
Given no overlap exists, when the system checks, then it confirms no conflict.
Trust: All conflict checks are logged with booking details.

stories.notes: Conflict detection logic already existed inline inside createBooking() since STORY-002; this story extracted it into its own explicit, reusable, independently-tested checkForConflict() function and added dedicated logging covering both outcomes (STORY-002 only ever logged the success/creation case, never the check itself). createBooking() now calls checkForConflict() rather than duplicating the overlap logic. All 3 named failure paths handled with dedicated tests: 'Missed conflict' (a real overlap is caught), 'False positive conflict' (a cancelled booking or a non-overlapping/adjacent time never falsely flags), 'Logging failure' (a broken logger cannot crash the check - wrapped in try/catch, verified via a test that makes console.log throw and confirms the check still returns the correct result). Refactoring this exposed a pre-existing test-hygiene issue in bookingsService.test.ts: two audit-logging tests used a manual logSpy.mockRestore() at the end of each test body, which never ran when an assertion failed partway through, leaking the spy's call history into the next test; fixed by switching to afterEach(() => jest.restoreAllMocks()). No frontend work - task guidance scopes this to 'the booking service', and the existing BookingForm (STORY-002) already surfaces conflict errors from its UI.

criteria.text: Given a customer requests a booking, when AI suggests times, then optimal times are presented.
Given a busy period, when AI analyzes, then it suggests alternative times.
Trust: All AI scheduling suggestions are logged with rationale.

stories.notes: Built as a deterministic, rules-based scheduling engine, not a real LLM/AI API integration - no credentials exist in this environment for one, and adding an external AI dependency is a decision flagged to the user rather than made unilaterally (per CLAUDE.md's Autonomy Model). Reasons over real booking data via checkForConflict (STORY-005): presents the preferred time when free; when busy, checks candidate alternatives (+/-1h, +/-2h, next day) against real bookings and returns only genuinely free ones, each suggestion logged with a rationale. Every candidate is re-verified before being offered, so 'never suggests an actually-busy time' holds by construction, not by luck. Frontend: BookingForm fetches suggestions on conflict and offers them as clickable pre-fills, per this story's task guidance to integrate with the booking interface. Found and fixed a real gap while testing: the frontend's fetchSuggestions only handled non-2xx HTTP responses, not the fetch() call itself failing (a genuine network-level 'Integration error') - this was silently unhandled until a dedicated test surfaced it. All 3 criteria verified via automated tests, manual curl + raw log inspection against a live server, and a live DOM check confirming the integrated page still renders correctly.

criteria.text: Given booking data, when AI analyzes, then trends are displayed on the dashboard.
Given a slow period, when AI analyzes, then it identifies the period.
Trust: All analytics reports are logged with data sources and timestamps.

stories.notes: Same 'AI' scope reasoning as STORY-003/006: deterministic engine, not a real LLM call. Groups confirmed bookings by day of week (UTC, deliberately - bookings are stored as UTC ISO strings, so classifying by local time would make results depend on which machine runs it) and classifies each day busy/slow/normal relative to the average across all 7 days. Correctness by construction: cancelled bookings never count toward a day's trend, and an all-empty or perfectly-even dataset is honestly 'normal' everywhere rather than a fabricated busy/slow label. Added listBookings() to bookingsService.ts as the read accessor this needed (same pattern as listEscalations/listSchedulingIssues). Manually seeded real bookings and verified the busy/slow math by hand before writing any tests (average = 4/7 - every count above it correctly flagged busy, every count below it correctly flagged slow). All 3 criteria and all 3 named failure paths verified via automated tests, live curl against real seeded data, and a live DOM check confirming the dashboard tab renders alongside the other four.

criteria.text: Given a complex query, when AI processes it, then a detailed response is provided.
Given an unsupported query, when AI processes it, then a fallback response is given.
Trust: All complex query interactions are logged with details.

tests_added: backend/src/services/assistantService.test.ts (answerQuestion — trends and complex queries (STORY-008) describe block)
stories.notes: Enhances STORY-003's assistant rather than building a parallel one — one Q&A entry point for customers, and REQ-005's own task line says 'enhance', not 'add'. Same honest-substitution AI-scope reasoning as STORY-003/006/007: no LLM/NLP credentials exist here, so this stays a deterministic keyword-matching engine, flagged explicitly. Adds a third topic (busy/slow trends), reusing STORY-007's generateAnalyticsReport() rather than rebuilding trend logic. Deliberately did NOT reuse STORY-006's scheduling suggestions - suggestBookingTimes() needs a specific field/time the assistant doesn't have from free text, and fabricating one to force a fit would itself risk the 'incorrect response' failure path. A 'complex query' is defined as one matching 2+ of {pricing, availability, trends}; matched parts are synthesized into one detailed answer (acceptance criterion 1), a fully unrecognized question keeps STORY-003's existing honest fallback (criterion 2, regression-tested), and every interaction still logs to console plus the audit trail exactly as before (criterion 3). New failure path this story introduces - 'NLP processing error' - is handled by graceful degradation, not a blanket 500: if the trends lookup throws (mocked and tested), any already-computed pricing/availability parts are still returned along with an honest note, rather than losing the whole answer, per CLAUDE.md's Failure-First Design fallback guidance. No frontend changes needed - AssistantPage.tsx already renders whatever answer comes back. Verified live via manual curl (seeded real Saturday-heavy bookings, confirmed the assistant's trends answer matches the raw analytics report byte-for-byte) before writing the 6 new automated tests. Backend: 130/130 tests across 17 suites (6 new), tsc clean.

criteria.text: Given a customer issue, when AI handles it, then the issue is resolved or escalated.
Given an escalated issue, when a human handles it, then the customer is informed of the outcome.
Trust: All customer service interactions are logged with resolution details.

stories.notes: Worked as a paced co-pilot again at the user's request - one confirmed step at a time. New backend/src/services/customerServiceService.ts orchestrates (not rebuilds) STORY-003/008's assistant and STORY-004's escalations: a refund/complaint is always escalated straight to a human (REQ-012 detection, never even asks the AI); anything else is tried against the assistant first, and anything it can't answer is escalated as a new 'general' EscalationType (REQ-015) instead of left as a dead-end decline. Deliberately kept this as a thin orchestration layer, not a new 'AI engine' - it calls the two already-built services rather than reimplementing either. Criterion 2 (customer informed of the outcome) required extending escalationsService.decideEscalation() itself, since that's where a human's decision actually lands: added customerNotifiedAt (in-app record, same honest-substitution pattern as STORY-012 - no real email/SMS exists here) plus a new GET /api/customer-service/issues/:id lookup so the customer can check it. While hardening the new notification step's failure path, found and fixed a real pre-existing gap from STORY-004: the original escalation_decided console.log was never wrapped in try/catch (every other log call in this codebase is) - a logging hiccup would have crashed the whole decision; fixed, and fixed two existing STORY-004 tests whose exact-call-count assumptions broke now that a decision logs twice (same 'filter by event name' fix as STORY-005). Also caught a second real regression from widening EscalationType: EscalationCard.tsx's label was a two-way ternary that silently mislabeled any non-refund escalation as 'Complaint' - replaced with an explicit mapping and added a regression test before it could ship broken. New 'Get Help' page (user's explicit choice over folding into the existing Assistant page) - separate from Ask-a-question because this is a genuinely different customer journey (submit-and-track vs. quick-answer). Three failure paths: 'AI handling error' falls back to escalating (a real, deterministic fallback exists, so it's used, per Failure-First Design) rather than losing the issue; 'Escalation failure' has no further fallback, so it fails honestly with a clear message and log, never a fabricated resolution; 'Customer notification failure' leaves customerNotifiedAt honestly null rather than silently pretending the customer was told, and never blocks the decision itself from being recorded.

criteria.text: Given the system is under normal load, when a user interacts with the system, then the response time is under 2 seconds.
Given the system is under peak load, when a user interacts with the system, then the response time is under 5 seconds.
Trust: Given a performance optimization is applied, when a user interaction occurs, then the interaction is logged in the audit trail.

stories.notes: Worked as a paced co-pilot again. This story's own cited requirements did not match this codebase: REQ-016/REQ-017 ask for real database connections, but every service here is an explicitly-scoped in-memory walking skeleton with no database anywhere - introducing one is a strategic/architectural decision this repo's own CLAUDE.md reserves for the user (Autonomy Model: 'Database engine or schema redesign' and 'External dependency introduction' are both ESCALATE, not PROCEED), so I flagged it rather than silently faking a DB connection to make the requirement text look satisfied. User confirmed: skip those two, build only the actual acceptance criteria. REQ-011 ('detect cancellations') was also flagged as already fully built (bookingsService.cancelBooking(), audit-logged, since STORY-011) - nothing new needed there, it just doesn't belong under a performance story. What was actually built: a version-stamped cache on analyticsService.generateAnalyticsReport() (the most expensive read in this system, hit from three places) - deliberately NOT a blind time-based TTL, since that could serve stale busy/slow trends right after a new booking (the same 'Incorrect trend identification' risk from STORY-007, just reintroduced by the optimization itself); instead keyed on a new bookingsVersion counter in bookingsService, bumped on every real create/cancel, so a cache hit is only ever served when nothing has actually changed. This required adding resetAnalyticsCache() and wiring it into three existing test files (analyticsService.test.ts, routes/analytics.test.ts, assistantService.test.ts's trends block) that reset bookings between tests but didn't know about the new cache - without this, a stale cached report from one test could have silently leaked into the next, since resetBookings() also resets the version counter back to the same value an earlier test cached against. Cache hits are now logged to the audit trail (widened entityType/action unions again, 'performance_optimization'/'cache_hit') for the Trust criterion, with its own failure-path test proving an audit-trail hiccup never breaks a cache hit. Criteria 1 & 2 (response time) are enforced by a real performance test against a genuinely seeded 500-booking dataset, not an empty one - a single request completed in 36ms (vs the 2s threshold) and 50 concurrent requests in 221ms (vs the 5s threshold), so there's real headroom, not a coincidental pass. Failure paths 1 & 2 ('fails to respond within time') don't have a separate mocked-failure test the way other stories' failure paths do - these are non-functional requirements, and the performance test itself is the enforcement mechanism, not something with a distinct broken-input scenario to construct; said this explicitly rather than force-fitting a synthetic test that wouldn't prove anything real. All 3 criteria and the one genuinely testable failure path (missing audit trail logs) verified via automated tests; 157/157 backend tests across 20 suites (up from 148: 6 new caching tests + 3 new performance tests), tsc clean.

criteria.text: Given a booking is made, when the booking is confirmed, then the booking details are recorded in the audit trail.
Given a booking is cancelled, when the cancellation is processed, then the cancellation details are recorded in the audit trail.
Trust: Given any booking action occurs, when the action is completed, then the action is logged with a timestamp in the audit trail.

stories.notes: No cancellation capability existed before this story (STORY-002 only ever built creation); added a minimal cancelBooking() as a necessary walking-skeleton prerequisite for auditing a cancellation action, since the acceptance criteria explicitly require one. Audit trail is a real structured, queryable store (recordAuditEntry/listAuditEntries), distinct from the console logging STORY-001/002/004 already do - that logging isn't 'accessible for verification' in any structured sense, this is, via GET /api/audit-trail. Both creation and cancellation are idempotent, and cancellation is idempotent-verified at the audit-trail level too: cancelling twice does not add a duplicate entry. No frontend UI built for this story - the acceptance criteria and task guidance are satisfied at the API level ('accessible for verification' = the GET endpoint), and unlike STORY-001/004 nothing here names a customer- or staff-facing page; the owning role is System Auditor, not a UI persona. All 3 criteria verified via automated tests plus manual curl checks (including confirming the audit trail entry count stayed at 2, not 3, after a repeat cancellation) against a live dev server.

criteria.text: Given a scheduling conflict exists, when the system detects it, then the scheduler is notified immediately.
Given a scheduling issue is resolved, when the resolution is confirmed, then the system updates the schedule accordingly.
Trust: Given a scheduling issue is detected, when the issue is logged, then it is recorded in the audit trail with details.

stories.notes: Last story in the plan. 'Notify the scheduler' built as an in-app, immediately-queryable notification list - no real email/SMS channel exists or has credentials, same honest-substitution pattern as STORY-006. Widened STORY-011's auditTrailService entityType/action unions ('booking' -> 'booking'|'scheduling_issue') to admit this story's entries - a natural extension of shared infrastructure, not a hack. Wired reportSchedulingConflict into bookingsService.createBooking()'s existing conflict branch (only on a genuine different-customer conflict, never on an idempotent retry), isolated in its own try/catch so a notification failure can never mask or break the customer-facing 409 rejection. Resolution is idempotent (resolving twice does not re-process) and removes the issue from the open list, which is this story's own reading of 'updates the schedule accordingly'. All 3 criteria and all 3 named failure paths verified via automated tests, manual curl through the full detect->notify->audit->resolve->idempotent-resolve lifecycle against a live server, and a live DOM check confirming all three nav tabs render.
